 COMMONJUDGMENT  These two claim petitions are filed by the respective petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the common respondents, claiming compensation with respect to the injuries sustained by petitioner in MVC 104/2023 and death of deceased K.N Sai Charan Shetty in MVC No.353/2023 in a road traffic accident. 
Nagajyothi K vs Bhuvaneswari S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76506239/
2  2. The above said petitions arose out of the same accident and the respondents in the said petitions are same. Hence, the above two petitions were clubbed and common evidence was recorded in MVC.104/2023 and hence the petitions are taken to pass common judgment. 
 3. The brief facts of petitions averments are that;
On 25-11-2022 at about 1-20 p.m., the petitioner Nagajyothi as a pillion rider in MVC No.104/2023 and the  SCCH-24 4 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023 deceased Charan Shetty in MVC No.353/2023 as a rider were proceeding in a motorcycle bearing No.AP-02-AU- 50221 and when they reached near Koduru Thopu, on NH-44 road, Hyderabad to Bangalore, Chilamathur, at that time the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-L-8798 came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed result of which the driver of the lorry lost control over his vehicle and came to the wrong side dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which the pillion rider and rider of the said vehicle sustained severe injuries all over the body and rider succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
 4. The petitioner in MVC.104/2023 soon after the accident was taken to Government Hospital, Hindupur and for better treatment she was taken to Aster CMI Hospital, Bangalore wherein admitted as an inpatient for 15 days and underwent below knee amputation left leg with primary closure, wound debridement and closure of back wound on 26-11-2022. Prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy; she was aged about 39 years and was doing business thereby earning more than Rs.50,000/- per moth. Due to the injuries sustained, she became disabled and she cannot do her normal work also and not in a position to do her work as before. 
 SCCH-24 5 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023  5. It is stated in MVC.353/2023 that deceased Charan Setty was aged about 19 years. He was hale and healthy prior to the accident and was doing business (Camphor, Candles and Match box business) and earning more than Rs.50,000/- per month. The petitioners are totally depending on the income of the deceased and they Nagajyothi K vs Bhuvaneswari S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76506239/
3 were finding extremely difficult to eke out their livelihood as the deceased was the only bread earner of their family. 
 6. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - Bhuvneswari S / the R.C. owner of lorry bearing reg.No.TN-52-L-8798 has remained absent hence he was placed ex-parte. 
 7. The respondent No.2/the Insurer of the lorry bearing reg.No.TN-52-L-8798 have filed written statement in both the cases and admitted the coverage of policy to the offending vehicle and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy. It is contended that the driver of insured vehicle was not holding valid driving license. It is further contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider/deceased of the motorcycle. It is further contended that the rider without having  SCCH-24 6 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023 knowledge of the riding, ride the vehicle in a zigzag manner in the middle of the road without wearing the helmet and that the said motorcycle was not having valid Insurance policy at the time of accident.
 8. On the basis of rival pleadings following common issues have been framed;
 Issue in MVC 104/2023  1. Whether the petitioner proves that she  had sustained grievous injuries in the  RTA alleged to have occurred on  25.11.2022 at about 01.20 p.m., near  Koduru Thopu on NH-44 road,
 Hyderabad to Bangalore, Chilamathur  Mandal, Sri.Sathys Sai District,
 Puttaparthy, A.P., due to rash and  negligent driving of the driver of Lorry  bearing Reg.No.TN-52-L-8798?
 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled fro  Compensation? If so, what is the  quantum? From whom? 
 3. What order or award? 
 Issue in MVC 353/2023 Nagajyothi K vs Bhuvaneswari S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76506239/ 
4  1. Whether the Petitioners prove that, they  are the legal heirs of the deceased  Sri.K.N.Sai Charan Setty? 
 2. Whether the Petitioners prove that,
 Sri.K.N.Sai Charan Setty was died on  SCCH-24 7 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023  account of road traffic accident on  25.11.2022 at about 1.20 p.m., near Koduru  Thopu on NH-44 road, Hyderabad to  Bangalore, Chilamathur Mandal, Sri.Sathys  Sai District, Puttaparthy, A.P., due to rash  and negligent driving of the driver of Lorry  bearing Reg.No.TN-52-L-8798 ?
 3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for  compensation as claimed? If so, what is  the quantum? From whom Payable? 
 4. What order or award? 
 9. Common evidence was recorded in MVC.104/2023. In order to prove the case of the petitioner in MVC No.104/2022 and in MVC No.353/2023 the petitioner no1 has examined herself as PW.1 and Pw.2 respectively and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14 and three witnesses is examined as PW.3 to PW.5 and got marked documents at Ex.P15 to P20. On the other hand, the respondent no.2 has not adduced any evidence on their behalf. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 has filed memo with policy same is marked as consent as Ex.R1.
 10. I have heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioners and the respondent no.2 in both the petitions and perused the entire materials placed on record. 
 SCCH-24 8 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023  11. My findings on the above issues in MVC 104/2023 are as follows;
 Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3: As per final order,
Nagajyothi K vs Bhuvaneswari S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76506239/
5  for the following;
 12. My findings on the above issues in MVC 353/2023 are as follows;
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3: As per final order,
 for the following;
 REASONS  13. Issue No.1 in MVC No.353/2023 : The petitioners have stated that they are the only legal representatives of the deceased. In support of their contention, they have produced Aadhaar card of the petitioners and deceased at Ex.P13 which shows that the petitioner No.1 is the mother and petitioner No.2 is the minor sister of the deceased. The respondents have not seriously disputed the relationship of deceased with petitioners. Hence petitioners are considered as the dependents of the deceased. Hence issue no1 in MVC No.356/2023 is answered in the affirmative. 
 SCCH-24 9 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023  14. Issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.104/2023 and Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.356/2023:- As these issues are interconnected they are taken up together for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts. 
 In order to substantiate that the accident in question has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-L-8798, the petitioner in MVC No.104/2023 got examined herself as PW.1 and Petitioner no.1 in MVC No.353/2023 got examined herself as PW.2. The PWs.1 and 2 has deposed in her chief examination that Pw.1 and deceased were proceeding in a motorcycle bearing No.AP-02-AU-50221 and when they reached near Koduru Thopu, on NH-44 road, Hyderabad to Bangalore, Chilamathur, at that time the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-52-L-8798 (herein after referred to as offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed result of which the driver of the lorry lost control over his vehicle and came on the wrong side and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle, result of which the pillion rider and rider of the said vehicle sustained severe injuries all over the body and rider succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
 SCCH-24 10 MVC 104/2023 Nagajyothi K vs Bhuvaneswari S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76506239/
6  C/w 353/2023  15. In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 and Pw2 has relied upon Ex.P1 to P4 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, translated copy of complaint, FIR , wound certificate, Accident report,
charge sheet etc.,
 16. On the basis of the complaint lodged by G.N.Savith, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No 165/2022 of Chilamathur Police Station for the offence punishable under section 337, 304-A of MV Act. The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 338, 304(A) of IPC.
 17. So far as the contention taken by the petitioners as to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle is concerned, the learned counsel for respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the said fact and contended that the deceased who was the rider of motorcycle bearing No.AP-02-AU- 5021 being minor having no driving license and having no insurance policy driven his vehicle in zigzag manner on the middle of the road without following the traffic rules  SCCH-24 11 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023 and caused for the accident hence deceased too has contributed negligence. Hence negligence on the part of the deceased is to be attributed at the ratio of 50:50.
 18. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 at this juncture has relied upon the judgment reported in (2018)
6 SCC 765 between Nishan Singh & Ors., Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., & Ors., wherein referring to the facts of the said case it was observed that "there was no evidence on record to indicate that the driver of offending vehicle suddenly applied his break in middle of road and there was no evidence regarding exact place of occurrence of accident in absence of any survey, therefore finding that truck was not driven rashly and negligently nor had been brought truck to center of road at right side or applied sudden break to cause accident.
Nagajyothi K vs Bhuvaneswari S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76506239/
7  19. In 2009 Supreme (SC) 995 between Raj Rani &
Ors, Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.Ld., & Ors., it was observed that "The question of contributory negligence arises when there has been some act or omission on the claimants part, which has materially contributed to the damage caused and is of such a nature that it may properly be described as 'negligence'. Negligence ordinarily means breach of a legal duty to care, but when  SCCH-24 12 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023 used in the expression "contributory negligence", it does not mean breach of any duty. It only means the failure by a person to use reasonable care for the safety of either himself or his property, so that he becomes blameworthy in part as an author of his own wrong".
 20. In the light of the submission made by the learned counsel for respondent no.2, if the materials placed on record is perused, as per the charge sheet, the deceased and PW.1 were proceeding in the motorcycle from Kodur Junction to Gorantla town and offending vehicle which was proceeding from Ananthapuram side to Bengaluru side dashed to the motorcycle of the deceased. 
In the FIR at Ex.P1 it is stated that the offending vehicle dashed to the scooter which was crossing towards left side. It means, at the time of accident deceased was taking turn of his vehicle. Even though respondent no2 has seriously disputed the manner of accident but very strangely for the reason best known to the petitioners they have not produced either the spot mahazar or sketch or IMV report. In cases of this nature in order to ascertain the rash and negligent act, the aforesaid three documents assume much importance and it plays a vital role. Based on the said three documents the Tribunal has to ascertain the rash and negligent aspect on the part of the  SCCH-24 13 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023 vehicles involved in the accident. The petitioners ought to have produced the said three documents. It is true that charge sheet is filed only against the driver of the offending vehicle but charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to prove the aforesaid material fact. The non production of the aforesaid three documents creates doubt in the mind of the court regarding truthness in the Nagajyothi K vs Bhuvaneswari S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76506239/
8 case of petitioners regarding their contention of sole negligence contributed by the driver of offending vehicle. 
If really deceased has not contributed any amount of negligence then there was no need for the petitioners to suppress the material documents from the notice of the court. Hence, when in the FIR it is stated that the deceased while crossing the road or to say while taking turn of the motorcycle met with an accident under such circumstances while taking turn of the vehicle the deceased too had to take precautionary measures. It is only after confirming that no vehicles are coming at the place where deceased was taking turn of the vehicle; he ought to have taken turn of his vehicle . Hence, from the materials placed on record it can be said that even deceased too has contributed negligence. The negligence contributed by the deceased can be assessed at 15%. 
Hence, petitioners have to forgo compensation to the  SCCH-24 14 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023 extent of 15% from the total compensation going to be awarded by the Tribunal. 
 21. So far as the submission made by the respondent no.2 regarding deceased riding the vehicle without driving license and that deceased was minor at the time of accident etc is concerned, if the Aadhar card of the deceased at Ex.P13 is perused his date of birth was 22-05-2004. It means as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 18 years 6 months 3 days. 
There are no materials placed on record to say that deceased was not holding valid driving license and that he was riding the vehicle without driving license and without wearing helmet. 
 22. In view of the observation made here in above this court is of the opinion that the deceased has contributed negligence to the extent of 15% and the driver of the offending vehicle has contributed negligence to the extent of 85%. Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in MVC No.104/2023 and Issue no.2 in MVC No.353/2023 in the partly affirmative. 
 23. Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.104/2023: P.W.1 has given evidence to the effect of her sustained severe injuries. As observed earlier, petitioner has produced  SCCH-24 15 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023 Nagajyothi K vs Bhuvaneswari S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76506239/
9 medical documents which are at Ex.P.2 and Ex.P5. On going through the medical documents it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient from 25-11- 2022 to 30-11-2022 at Aster CMI Hospital, Bengaluru for a period of 6 days and underwent below knee amputation on 26-11-2022. As per wound certificate the petitioner has sustained one injury which is grievous in nature. 
 24. Dr.S.A Somashekara - Orthopedic Surgeon at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospitals, Bangalore has given evidence as Pw4 and produced OPD record with examination report and recent X-ray at Ex.P.18 and 19. 
P.W.4 has deposed that he examined the petitioner clinically and radiologically as to the assessment of disabilities. PW.4 further deposed that the petitioner has suffered below knee amputation and suffered disability of left lower limb at 75% and on whole body at 55%. PW.2 further deposed that petitioner needs sophisticated lower limb prosthesis which is expensive and runs in lakh. 
 25. Considering the nature of injuries sustained,
period of treatment taken, and this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads. 
 SCCH-24 16 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023  26. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained grievous injury. In a judgment rendered by the hon'ble High court in MFA No 1914/2017 between Saleem Whammed and Ors/ The National Insurance Company Ltd and Others where minor aged 7 years sustained injury in a road traffic accident and her left leg was amputated below the knee and artificial limb was fixed. In the given set of facts the hon'ble High court has awarded compensation under the head pain and suffering to the tune of Rs 2,00,000/- . 
 27. In the present case the petitioner who was aged about 39 years sustained grievous injury and her left side below knee is amputed. Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards pain and suffering. 
 28. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the Nagajyothi K vs Bhuvaneswari S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76506239/
10 petitioner is concerned, she has produced 17 medical bills as per Ex.P.8 for Rs.4,10,695/-. The respondents have not raised serious dispute regarding the genuineness of medical bills. If medical bills are calculated it comes around Rs.4,10,600/- Under such circumstances the  SCCH-24 17 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023 petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,10,600/- under the head medical expenses.
 29. It is stated that petitioner was doing business and thereby earning more than Rs.50,000/- per month. 
But to substantiate the said contention the petitioner has not produced any documents. Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of petitioner etc considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/- p.m.
 30. The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and taken treatment for 6 days as inpatient in Aster CMI Hospital, Bengaluru. Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature, it is reasonable to hold that period of three months as complete laid down period. Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.15,500/-
p.m for three months. Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.46,500/- towards loss of income during the laid down period. 
 SCCH-24 18 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023  31. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, the petitioner has taken treatment for several times. Further for 6 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment. She has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses. Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.20,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2022. 
 32. P.W.4 deposed that the petitioner has suffered below knee amputation and she suffered physical disability of 55% on whole body. 
Nagajyothi K vs Bhuvaneswari S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76506239/
11  33. It is stated by the petitioner that at the time of accident the petitioner was aged about 39 years. In this regard, petitioner has produced Aadhar card/ Ex.P.7 which shows her date of birth as 13-06-1983. As accident took place in the year 2022, it can be said that deceased was aged about 39 years as on the date of accident. 
 34. So far as assessing the compensation under different heads, the learned counsel for PW.1 has relied upon judgment reported in 2023 ACJ 2773 between  SCCH-24 19 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023 Rajesh Singh Vs. Sheik Mohammed Omar & Anr . In the said case, right leg below knee of the petitioner was amputed. The petitioner was working as helper on a crane suffered disability at 40%. The Hon'ble High Court by relying upon the income fixed by Karnataka Legal State Authority took the income, added 40% of the income towards future prospects and taken functional disability at 60%. It has ordered Rs.3,00,000/- for artificial limb. 
 35. The honb'le Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No 9070-9071 of 2022 arising out of special leave petition no 481-482 of 2019 decided on 9/12/2022 between Mohd.
Sabeer / Regional Manager UP State Road Transport Corporation. In the said case injured petitioner was scrap dealer doing self business. The petitioner has suffered an amputation of lower right limb, a fracture in the medial wall of the bilateral orbit, crush injury on right leg,
fracture tibia right leg exposed vessels and other injuries. 
As per disability certificate the petitioner has suffered 70%
of disability but the Hon'ble high court has held that petitioner has only 35% of loss in future earning duty to the disability. Under the given set of facts the hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "to assess the quantum of compensation to be awarded the court has to assess whether the permanent disability caused has any adverse  SCCH-24 20 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023 effect on the earning capacity of the petitioner. In the said case the petitioner was not salaried person but is self employed who manages his business. It was observed by the hon'ble Supreme court that "For the petitioner to be Nagajyothi K vs Bhuvaneswari S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76506239/
12 able to augment his income he is most defiantly required to move around, he can also not drive on his own which hinders his mobility further, this proves that the functional disability of the petitioner will severally impact on his earning capacity and the hon'ble Supreme court has assessed the loss of future earning capacity of the petitioner at 60%. 
 36 . It was also held that in cases of permanent disablement caused by a motor accident, the claimant is entitled to not just future loss of income but also future prospects. It is observed by the hon'ble Supreme Court that the just compensation must be interpreted in such a manner as to place the claimant in the same position as he was before the accident took place. Hence referring the judgment reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 National Insurance company Limited / Pranay Sethi and Ors the hon'ble Apex court has given 40% addition of future prospects as compensation.
 SCCH-24 21 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023  37. In MFA No 201582 of 2017 (MV -1) decided on 10/8/2023 between The Manager United India Insurance Company Ltd/ Srinivas and Ors. In the said case so far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the honb'le High court referring the medical records observed that when the right hand upper 1/3rd of elbow of the petitioner has been amputed and doctor has assessed the permanent disability of 80% , it has taken the disability of petitioner to the whole body as 80% . 
 38. In MFA No 1234/2014 and 2414/2014 (WC)
between Hanumathappa / Shriram General Insurance company Ltd decided on 2/12/2022, the right hand of the driver / petitioner was amputed. The doctor has assessed the disability of the petitioner at 85% and the doctor who amputed the right upper limb has also been examined as Pw3 and the photographs which have been produced before the court discloses that his right hand was amputed. Hence it was observed by the Hon'ble High court that the commissioner has rightly taken the disability of the petitioner at 80%. 
 39. In the facts of the case in MFA No 1914 /2017 Saleem Ahammed and Ors / The National Insurance Company Ltd and Ors, the left leg of the minor petitioner was amputed and doctor has assessed the disability of  SCCH-24 22 MVC 104/2023 Nagajyothi K vs Bhuvaneswari S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76506239/
13  C/w 353/2023 petitioner at 50%. Hence the court has taken the disability of the petitioner as 50%. 
 40. In all the cases above referred the court has considered the percentage of disability assessed by the doctor and while assessing the loss of income due to disability, future prospect is added. 
 41. So taking in to consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.15,500/- p.m, when left below knee was amputed and as petitioner was doing business, with the said percentage of disability she cannot continue her work and hence, it is appropriate to assess the disability of 45% on whole body. 
When the notional income of the petitioner is assessed at Rs.15,500/-, if 40% is added towards future prospects, it comes to Rs.21,700/-. When the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 39 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 36 to 40 is 15. So by applying multiplier '15' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.17,57,700/-
(Rs.21,700 x 45 %x15 x 12 ). Hence this Tribunal holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.17,57,700/- towards future loss of income due to disability including future prospect. 
 SCCH-24 23 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023  42. So far as cost of artificial limb and its maintenance is concerned it is deposed by Pw4 that petitioner is advised to have below Knee Prosthesis which is expensive and runs in to lakhs. The Pw5- Immanuel, a Sr.Prosthetist holding position of Managing Direction of John's Prosthetic and Orthotic Center produced Quotation of Prosthetic and Orthotic Center at Ex.P.20. It is deposed by Pw.5 that the petitioner visited their hospital on 19-01- 2024 for a below knee Prosthesis. Pw.5 further deposed that he examined the petitioner's stump and muscle power and recommend her for prosthesis which will enable her for K3 & K4 activity and it will enable her to do all normal basic day today activities. 
 43. PW.5 further deposed that the total cost of fitment of below knee prosthesis with Echelon foot and Nagajyothi K vs Bhuvaneswari S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76506239/
14 with silicon socket will be costing her around Rs.7,20,930/-, that the above said prescribed prosthesis has 3 years warranty and the same can be used for up to 8-10 years without any problem depends upon the maintenance. 
 44 . PW.5 further deposed that the socket of the prosthesis need to be changed if there is any variation happens in her stump i.e., size and volume of the stump. 
 SCCH-24 24 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023 The maintenance charge for prosthesis including socket,
silicon, fairing and cover fabric per bi-annual will be casting around Rs.55,000/-. Pw.5 further deposed that depends upon the wear and tear the components and the damaged parts need to change once in 8 years. 
 45 . In judgment in Mohd. Sabeer / Regional Manager UP State Road Transport Corporation where in the hon'ble supreme court has awarded sum of Rs.7,80,000/- for purchase of three prosthetic limb in his life time and for maintenance of the same he was awarded an additional compensation of Rs 5,00,000/-. In the said case the injured was aged about 37 years but in the present case the petitioner at the time of accident was aged about 39 years and now she is aged about 41 years. 
 46 . Hence keeping in mind the observation made in the aforesaid rulings wherein injured was compensated to purchase three prosthetic limbs in her life time and awarded compensation of Rs.7,80,000/- for purchase of three prosthetic, it is just to award compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- for purchase of 3 prosthetic limbs in the life time of petitioner at a cost of Rs.2,50,000/- each and awards compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- for maintenance of the same till the life time of the petitioner  SCCH-24 25 MVC 104/2023  C/w 353/2023  47. The petitioner at her age of 39 years has lost her lower left limb below the knee, for that artificial limb has to be fixed. Hence considering the pathetic condition of the petitioner it is just to award compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Nagajyothi K vs Bhuvaneswari S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76506239/
15 Rs.1,50,000/-. Accordingly the petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:

 2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 20,000/-
 charges and nourishing food  3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 46,500/-
 laid up period  4. Future Loss of Income and future Rs.17,57,700/-

 6. Cost of artificial limb and its Rs.11,00,000/-
